suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Shuttle seat
suggested_services.example: The main story: a $35 round-trip seat on Lee Care Shuttle's Saturday run, out at 11:00am and back at 3:00pm, paid in full when booking. An accessible seat (a wheelchair space) is $55.

suggested_services.name: Shuttle seat
suggested_services.example: A senior living community books $35 seats for its residents. Nothing is taken when it books, and Rosie texts the community one bill a month.

suggested_services.name: Door-to-door ride
suggested_services.example: The main story: Frank's door-to-door ride (a wheelchair van) out to an appointment, Thu Oct 22, pickup at 8:00am. $65 base + $3.50 a mile for 12 miles: $107. A card is saved, and it's charged when Dev texts DONE at the drop-off. The ride home is a second booking.

suggested_services.name: Door-to-door ride
suggested_services.example: A nursing home books a resident's ride on its facility account. Nothing is taken at booking, and Rosie texts the facility one bill a month.

suggested_services.name: Door-to-door ride
suggested_services.example: A rider who pays the company by cash, check or invoice. Nothing is taken at booking, and Lee Medical Rides bills its own way. Rosie sends nothing about money.

suggested_services.name: Door-through-door ride
suggested_services.example: A stretcher ride: $175 base + $5 a mile for 20 miles, $275. Sam reads the rider's needs, prices it and OKs it. A card is saved, and it's charged when the crew texts DONE.

before_times: Where the pickup is (a home or a facility) and the town
Where the ride goes: the town only. The place's name goes on the secure page
The appointment time (it sets the pickup time)
One way or round trip, and the time for the return
What help the ride needs: curb to curb, door to door, or a stretcher
after_time: The rider's own mobile, or a caregiver's
Who meets the driver at the destination and back home, if the rider can't be left alone
Which door, gate or entrance to use
secure_page_only: The destination's name and suite, and the kind of appointment
How the rider gets around, weight range when it decides the equipment, and oxygen or other equipment the rider brings
Memory or behavior notes and the named adult at each end
The facility's account, if a facility books
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult rider for themselves. A family member, guardian or caregiver for the rider, with the rider's own name and mobile on the booking. A facility's discharge planner or social worker for a patient. A rider under 18 is booked by a parent or guardian and rides only with an adult.

stop: a fall with a possible broken bone
anyone who needs medical care right now
go_on: The rider brings their own portable oxygen: booked; the tank is secured, nobody smokes, and the driver never adjusts it.
Memory loss, confusion or a fall risk: booked door through door, with a named adult at both ends.
Ice or an unsafe step at the door: the driver may refuse the step, and waits while it's made safe; the owner calls and the ride moves with no fee.
stop_action: A medical emergency: 'Call 911 now. This is a ride service, not an ambulance.' No booking until they're safe.
Suicide or self-harm: 'Call or text 988 now; call 911 if anyone is in danger right now.' The ride waits until they say they're safe right now; the owner is told, never the words.

A rider who needs medical care or monitoring during the ride (an IV running, a ventilator the rider can't manage alone, a heart monitor, a medicine given on the way), or who can't sit up when the company has no stretcher service: not booked. 'This ride needs an ambulance. Your doctor's office or the hospital can arrange one.'
A rider who becomes ill or hurt during a ride: the driver pulls over safely and calls 911 first, stays, and gives no care beyond what the dispatcher asks. Then the owner tells the emergency contact.

prep: Be ready 15 minutes before the pickup time, at the door you named
Bring your ID and anything the appointment asked for
A power chair: charged, with the footrests on
Oxygen: enough for the whole trip and the wait
first_steps_and_forms.good_for: A ride details form stays good for 12 months, or until the rider's needs change.

skills: CPR and first aid (the company's rule, and where the state's rules require it)
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each driver: a driver's license for the vehicle (a commercial license with a passenger endorsement where federal or state rules require it), background and driving-record checks where the state's rules require them, and drug and alcohol testing where federal or state rules require it. No professional person license.
staff.supervision: A stretcher ride always has two crew. A new driver rides along with a trained driver first.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs stretcher rides, bariatric rides, facility accounts and every fee, and sets each driver's skills. The office manager may OK prices too; the owner's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: Riders book a ride, not a named driver. Any driver with the same skill and the right vehicle may take it, and the rider is told the driver's name. A stretcher ride needs two crew, or the owner calls.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult rider for themselves. A family member, guardian or caregiver for the rider, with the rider's own name and mobile on the booking. A facility's discharge planner or social worker for a patient. A rider under 18 is booked by a parent or guardian and rides only with an adult.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A minor's texts go to the parent or guardian. Nobody under 18 books.

visit.check_in: At pickup, the rider (or the adult meeting the driver) gives the check-in code at the door or at the van. At a facility, the desk hands the rider over and the code is given.
visit.done: DONE when the rider is dropped at the last address and, for a rider who can't be left alone, handed to the named adult. Then the saved card is charged for that ride.
visit.changes_at_visit: An extra stop, waiting or extra help asked for during the ride: priced first, and the payer says yes. It is paid at the drop-off with the ride, never before.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Where the state's rules or the local for-hire authority require it: a non-emergency medical transport permit or certificate for the company, with each vehicle inspected and listed. Stretcher rides only where the state's rules allow them outside an ambulance license. Elsewhere, the business registration.
license.who: The company holds the permit, the vehicle inspections and the insurance. Each driver holds a driver's license for the vehicle and passes the checks below.
license.ask: The permit or certificate number, where the state's form asks for one. The vehicle list: type, seats, wheelchair spaces, plate and inspection date. Proof of commercial auto insurance. Any USDOT number.
license.insurance: Commercial auto liability at the level the state's rules set. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Every driver: a background check and a driving-record check where the state's rules require them, and always as the example company's own rule. Drug and alcohol testing where federal or state rules require it.

never_in_a_text: The destination's name, the kind of appointment, a diagnosis, medicines
How the rider gets around, weight, oxygen and memory notes
